about: Claims shown on the Answer Checkers page. status keeps the research note's mark: verified = (V) primary text read; unverified = (U); inferred = (I) the note author's inference; ours = our own design, code or data. Every claim comes from 'Faithfulness Checkers - MiniCheck and HHEM - Research Note' (section in 'note'), except c53b and c64-c66 (our recount of pilot data files).

claims.text: MiniCheck takes a (document, claim) pair and returns a score in [0,1]; a threshold (default 0.5) turns it into supported or unsupported. Claims are single sentences.
The paper frames the task as document-level textual entailment with a binary label: contradiction and neutral both map to unsupported.
Backbones: RoBERTa-large (355M, from the AlignScore checkpoint, 14K synthetic examples only), DeBERTa-v3-large (355M) and Flan-T5-large (770M); the last two use 35K examples.
Training data: 21K ANLI examples plus 14K synthetic examples made with GPT-4/GPT-3.5 (C2D and D2C) that teach checking every atomic fact and combining sentences.
Models trained only on NLI data score 61.0 (T5-NLI-Mixed 11B) and 61.4 (FT5-ANLI-L) on LLM-AggreFact, below MiniCheck-FT5 at 74.7.
LLM-AggreFact BAcc averages: GPT-4 75.3, Claude-3 Opus 74.1, MiniCheck-FT5 74.7, MiniCheck-DBTA 72.6, MiniCheck-RBTA 72.7, AlignScore 70.4, SummaC-ZS 67.9, SummaC-CV 62.1.
Inference cost on the 13K test set: MiniCheck-FT5 $0.24 vs GPT-4 $107.
LLM-AggreFact uses 10 datasets in the paper and 11 later (RAGTruth added); metric balanced accuracy; threshold fixed at 0.5 for every model, tuning gives qualitatively similar results.
Claim decomposition gave no consistent gain and cost 2-4 times more; the model gives no explanation or span localisation.
Released code: max_model_len 2048 for FT5 and DeBERTa, 512 for RoBERTa; default chunk size 500 tokens for FT5, 400 for RoBERTa and DeBERTa. Longer premises are chunked.
HHEM-2.1-Open: input (premise, hypothesis), output a score 0-1; base model flan-t5-base; licence Apache-2.0; the card says unlimited context length (HHEM-1.0 was capped at 512 tokens).
Vendor speed figure: less than 600MB RAM at 32-bit and about 1.5 s for a 2k-token input on a modern x86 CPU (not checked independently).
FaithJudge lists HHEM-2.1-Open as 110M parameters; flan-t5-base itself is larger, so 110M probably counts only part of the model.
HHEM training data is not published: 'specific training details remain confidential'; it 'was trained using the RAGTruth summary training set among other datasets'.
There is no HHEM paper; the card gives a @misc citation.
Card table, balanced accuracy: RAGTruth-Summ 64.42 vs GPT-4 62.62; RAGTruth-QA 74.28 vs 74.11; AggreFact-SOTA 76.55 vs 73.78. Correctly quoted, but vendor numbers, not checked as true.
Because RAGTruth training data was used for HHEM-2.1-Open, its RAGTruth rows may not be a clean held-out test.
The Vectara Hallucination Leaderboard uses HHEM-2.3, Vectara's commercial model, so its numbers are not reproducible with HHEM-2.1-Open.

FaithBench BAcc / F1-macro: HHEM-2.1-Open 51.37 / 32.40; HHEM-2.1 (commercial) 55.68 / 40.86; MiniCheck-RoBERTa-L 55.03 / 53.35; MiniCheck-DeBERTa-L 54.95 / 54.90; MiniCheck-Flan-T5-L 50.50 / 49.52; GPT-4o zero-shot 56.29 / 40.75.
FaithBench was built from articles where HHEM and other detectors disagreed, so its numbers are biased downward for HHEM.
In RAGTruth, claims that need 2-3 hops are common; MiniCheck's D2C synthetic claims are 71.0% one-hop and 0.0% five-hop or more.
That one-hop training data limits detection of multi-hop claims is a hypothesis, not a test of MiniCheck itself.
Six factual-consistency metrics under seven meaning-preserving perturbations give inconsistent scores on long documents.
AlignScore, UniEval and MiniCheck show the highest instability in that study.
Fine-grained continuous scores are more reliable than binary classification for comparing evaluators on long-document summaries.
The HHEM card flags 'factual but hallucinated' on purpose: the hypothesis 'Paris is the capital of France' against a premise that says Berlin. The checker tests the text, not the world.
Asymmetry: 'I visited Iowa' is unsupported by 'I visited the United States', but not the reverse.

GraphEval splits LLM output into knowledge-graph triples and runs an NLI checker (HHEM, TRUE, TrueTeacher) on each triple; it reads the HHEM score at 0.5. It describes HHEM-1.0 as DeBERTaV3-based, trained on NLI data and fine-tuned on FEVER, Vitamin C and PAWS.
SummaC aggregates sentence-level NLI scores between document and summary sentences; 74.4 BAcc on its own 6-dataset benchmark; 67.9 (ZS) and 62.1 (CV) on LLM-AggreFact.

TRUE: 11 datasets (summaries, dialogue, fact verification, paraphrase); NLI and QG-QA metrics are 'strong and complementary'; it names filtering inconsistent outputs and augmenting training data as uses.
AlignScore: one alignment function trained on 4.7M examples from 7 tasks, RoBERTa 355M; 70.4 on LLM-AggreFact in the MiniCheck paper; MiniCheck-RBTA starts from it.
RAGTruth: about 18,000 RAG responses (QA, data-to-text, summaries) with word-level labels. It is a corpus, not a checker.
LLM-AggreFact leaderboard: 42 models, 14 shown by default; BAcc averages as in the table on this page.
For rows outside the 14 shown by default, the average is the mean of the 11 dataset scores, computed by the note's author with the page's rule.
Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B: same recipe (21K ANLI + 14K synthetic made by Llama-3.1-405B), fine-tuned from InternLM2.5-7B-chat, one sentence per claim, no chunking below 32K tokens; licence CC BY-NC 4.0.
Granite Guardian 3.3-8B has a groundedness criterion for RAG; card scores LLM-AggreFact 0.761 (no think) and 0.765 (think), TRUE 0.777 and 0.773; licence Apache-2.0.

Lynx is a Llama-3 fine-tune (8B and 70B) that reads (question, document, answer) and outputs PASS or FAIL with reasoning; CC BY-NC 4.0; not on LLM-AggreFact. On HaluBench: Lynx 70B 87.4%, Lynx v1.1 8B 84.3%, GPT-4o 86.5%.
Lynx is trained on the same sources as HaluBench, so HaluBench is an in-distribution test for it.
RAGAS faithfulness, an LLM judge, scores 66.9% on HaluBench.
Mid-size LLM judges score below the 0.8B MiniCheck-FT5 on the board: Llama-3.1-8B 70.3, Qwen2.5-7B 72.8; only frontier or 70B+ judges reach 75-77.
The board reports no confidence intervals, so a 1-point gap is not a proven difference.
FactCG adds multi-hop claims made from a document graph (CG2C) to the MiniCheck recipe; FactCG-DeBERTa-L (0.4B, MIT) scores 75.6 on the board; the authors report beating GPT-4o on LLM-AggreFact.
The MiniCheck-Flan-T5-Large card gives the licence MIT; our backend's docstring says Apache-2.0 (a doc fix, not done).
HaluBench: 15K samples from HaluEval, RAGTruth, FinanceBench, DROP, CovidQA, PubMedQA, as (question, context, answer); metric accuracy.
None of these benchmarks contains lecture slides, equations or tutoring answers; our own human-labelled dev pairs are the only in-domain test.

Our tutor runs MiniCheck-Flan-T5-Large as abstention layer 3: it splits the answer into sentences and checks each against the passages it cites ([n] markers); a sentence without a marker is checked against all cited passages. The premise is those passages joined into one input, never chunked; above the 2,048-token cap the sentence is 'unchecked'. Formulas are first turned into words; a formula-only sentence is 'not checkable'.
In hybrid mode the premise passages come from both the text arm and the graph arm; the graph arm returns the passages attached to the concepts it reaches. MiniCheck never sees a bare graph edge.
HHEM-2.1-Open runs on the same pairs but is logged only. support_check_mode = off | async | sync; in sync, an answer with no supported sentence becomes 'no answer'.
At KG-build time each graph assertion's evidence has HHEM and MiniCheck scores (a pre-check inside another system).

A sentence supported only by a graph edge with no text is flagged unsupported. The flag is correct but hides the graph's role; the fix is to add the edge's evidence quote or a verbalised triple to the premise.
Our answer prompt tells the model to derive results with standard mathematics; a derived step is not written in any passage, so the checker will often flag it. Count these as 'needs review'.
Five or more cited passages can pass 2,048 tokens and leave the sentence unchecked.

On 390 KG evidence claims of the pilot, HHEM supported 326 and MiniCheck 175, and they differed on 155 of all 390, or 104 of the 319 checked USES/IS_A claims (recounted from the pilot file; the note now says the same).

Our recount of the pilot data file: HHEM 326 and MiniCheck 175 of 390 at 0.5 (match); the 104 disagreements are among the 319 gated claims (USES and IS_A); over all 390 claims the checkers disagree on 155.
Our smoke test: 3 of 4 correct answers were flagged before formulas were turned into words.
Use A, faithfulness metric: RAGAS faithfulness is LLM-based.
ARES trains small judges for 'answer faithfulness'.

Use B, baseline: LLM-AggreFact lists AlignScore, SummaC, T5-NLI-Mixed and GPT-4 next to MiniCheck; FaithBench and FaithJudge list HHEM and MiniCheck; RAGTruth assesses several existing detection methods.
A baseline must get the same data, budget and tuning effort as the method; the MiniCheck paper fixes the threshold at 0.5 for every model for this reason.

In the thesis the text arm R (BM25 + dense + reranker) is the strong baseline for the graph arm H; closed-book L is the trivial baseline; Hc (H-collapsed) is an ablation baseline. In the product HHEM is a logged comparison checker for MiniCheck.

Product: keep MiniCheck-Flan-T5-L as the deciding checker; try FactCG-DeBERTa-L logged only beside it and switch only if it wins on labelled dev pairs from our own domain; Granite Guardian 3.3-8B as an offline second opinion on a GPU; do not ship Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B or Lynx (CC BY-NC 4.0); add graph evidence to the premise; show flags as 'needs review'.

Thesis: report the MiniCheck support rate per arm (R, H, Hc) as a descriptive secondary measure, HHEM beside it, and where they disagree; never as the primary outcome. The cut-off on our lecture text is an open calibration question (0.5 is a placeholder); the primary endpoint never uses a checker score.
claims.note: Recommendation; protocol 'Evaluation settings adopted' and decisions D7 (no author labelling)

claims.text: H answers join more passages than R answers, and MiniCheck is weaker on multi-hop claims, so the checker may under-rate H compared with R: a threat to validity.
The gap from MiniCheck-FT5 (75.0) to the best open-weight checker (77.4) is about 2.4 points; FactCG-DeBERTa-L is 0.6 points above at half the size.

Touch part 1 data: three pilot answers (Q17, Q18, Q20), three BM25 passages each, HHEM and MiniCheck scores of every sentence against every single passage and the ALCE citation-recall verdict against the cited passages joined. Model outputs.
Touch part 2 data: 390 KG pilot claim sentences, each scored by HHEM and MiniCheck against its whole passage.
MiniCheck outputs cluster at the extremes of the range.

In the thesis, MiniCheck (whole premise in one input, up to 2,048 tokens, never truncated at 512) and HHEM (robustness score only) are secondary grounding metrics; they never touch the primary endpoint (fully-correct rate, McNemar).
